title: The host payload ships the installed read handler and an installed-implementation catalog; `ia host` records a join and `ia doctor` reports both
summary: @inventarch/cli's embedded host payload now carries @inventarch/agent-composition-system and its dependency closure as a payload root, inside the payload and not as a CLI dependency (no host app imports it), plus a generated, inventoried implementations.json in format ia.installed-implementations.v1. Its evaluators section is an ia-evaluator-catalog/1.0 value with no installed entries, the built-ins being implicit. Its operations section lists captured-source-read-v1 as available, with its descriptor version, operation identity authoring-system/binding/operation/read-captured-source, handler ia.captured-source.read.v1, input and output validator ids, the payload path of the shipped handler module (agent-composition-system's dist/installed-read.js), that module's SHA-256, the installed packages of its closure and a closure digest over every shipped file of those packages; a first-party implementation whose package is not installed, or whose handler module is not built, imports a module that is not shipped or imports a package outside its shipped package closure, when the payload is generated is listed as unavailable with the reason and never as available. @inventarch/distribution adds the ./implementations subpath (and ./internal/implementations), exporting readInstalledImplementations(directory, release), installedImplementationsValue, closureDigest, readJoins, joinHost and leaveHost with their types, and INSTALLED_IMPLEMENTATIONS, INSTALLED_IMPLEMENTATIONS_FORMAT, INSTALLED_IMPLEMENTATIONS_ID, JOINS and JOINS_FORMAT. readInstalledImplementations reads the catalog only through the release pin, the inventory digest and the catalog digest, then checks each available operation against the bytes the payload ships: a handler module or closure package the inventory does not list, or a listed file that is absent, makes it unavailable, and handler or closure bytes or catalog pins that disagree with the inventory refuse with IA-DIST-INTEGRITY-MISMATCH; a v1 payload, or a v2 payload whose inventory lists no catalog (every payload built before this change, including the one 2.0.0 ships), reads as unavailable rather than damaged, and verifyHostCache is unchanged. joinHost records, under the host lock and after the pending-journal check, one row per consumer in .ia/distributions/hosts/joins.json (format ia.host-joins.v1: consumer, implementation installed-implementations, payload version, catalog digest, payload release and consumer revision), derived from the committed <host>-workspace.json registration and the catalog of the payload it names, and drops that row when there is no registration or no catalog; receipts that cannot be read refuse rather than being replaced. ia host claude|codex --apply, and so ia init --host, records the host's join after its MCP registration commits, with the workspace's authored revision as the consumer revision, and a removal drops it; a failure there names the rerun that finishes the set. ia doctor adds an implementations row for the catalog of the payload this installation pins in the IA home (ok when present, warn when it lists an unavailable operation, info when the payload carries none or is not materialized, fail when it fails verification), one join-<host> row per recorded join (ok when it names the catalog of the payload that host's registration uses, warn when it is drifted or the host is not registered, unknown when that catalog cannot be read), an info row for a registered host with no join, and a fail row for receipts that cannot be read; doctor still writes nothing. Limits: nothing imports, loads, executes or serves an operation, and no `@execution-binding` or `@check` binds to the catalog yet (milestone 7 runs operations); the catalog lists no installed evaluator; a join records which catalog a host registration joined, not that any handler ran; the payload grows by the composition package's files; the ia host --json envelope and its human output are unchanged.
